newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-PONTING FAILS AS TASMANIA STRUGGLE TO 288-8.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PONTING FAILS AS TASMANIA STRUGGLE TO 288-8.

text.p: Former test batsmen Ricky Ponting fell for just eight runs as Tasmania struggled to reach 288 for eight on the first day of their Sheffield Shield match against Western Australia in Hobart on Friday.

Ponting, who is bidding for a recall to the national side and a place in the squad for the tour to South Africa in February and March, was caught at mid-wicket off the fast bowling of Jo Angel as the Tasmanian batsmen battled an unpredictable Hobart pitch and a determined West Australian attack.
Ponting was dropped from the Australian side after the second test against West Indies in December.
After winning the toss and electing to bat, Tasmania began the match well, reaching 120 by lunch with the loss of just one wicket.
Opener Jamie Cox (96) and number three Michael DiVenuto (65) scored freely but DiVenuto went soon after the lunch break, followed by Ponting and captain David Boon for 15 as the visitors struck back.
Moody claimed the crucial wicket of Cox, who has made 795 runs this season at an average of 66.25, while Angel picked up another wicket to finish with 3-59 off 17 overs.
